also: as soon as it was dark

terms.gloss: at nightfall, as soon as it was dark
terms.grammar: ablative of time: “at the first darkness”
evidence: Liv. 31.23.4: classem in statiōne ūsque ad noctem tenuit: prīmīs tenebrīs mōvit (Lewis & Short s.v. tenebrae)
Liv. 45.6: prīmīs tenebrīs solvit nāvem (Lewis & Short s.v. solvō)
Cic. Att. 4.3.4: in comitium Milō dē nocte vēnit (Lewis & Short s.v. dē)
terms.comment: Dē nocte is “during the night, at night, by night” (Lewis & Short s.v. dē), often of getting up or setting out while it is still night (surgunt dē nocte latrōnēs, Hor. Ep. 1.2.32, Lewis & Short; see night). It says that something happens in the night, not that it follows nightfall; for “as soon as it was dark”, prīmīs tenebrīs.

sources: Lewis & Short: tenebrae · Lewis & Short: de
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
